title: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents

target_networks.name: multi-reflection SLM optical neural network (two phase masks phi1, phi2)

domain: optics / physical neural network hardware (vision: MNIST digits 0-2, Fashion-MNIST encoder)
tasks_benchmarks: MNIST digits 0/1/2 optical classification (3,147 test digits)
Fashion-MNIST optical encoder (16 detectors, PSNR on 300 test images)

headline_result.text: With notes from an earlier session, the Opus 5.5 agent trained the optical classifier on hardware to 96.8% test accuracy (91.1% without notes), versus about 52% for PPO and policy gradient and 96.3% for backpropagation through a calibrated model.
headline_result.quote: In contrast, our agent reached 91.1% from the task description alone, and 96.8% when it was given the notes and code of an earlier session, without any phase masks (Fig. 2b).

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: best run per method reported; three classifier runs with notes or lessons (89.2, 91.3, 96.8%); one encoder run per row

key_claims.claim: The method is framed as an extension of weight-space programming to physical networks whose parameters can only be measured.
key_claims.quote: A recently reported ability of these models, weight-space programming, is of particular interest for neural networks.35

key_claims.claim: Gradient-free baselines (PPO, policy gradient), tuned on the calibrated model over 22 settings, improved test accuracy only from 35% to about 52%.
key_claims.quote: Their settings were first searched in simulation and the best deployed on the experiment (Methods), where they improved the test accuracy from 35% to about 52%.

key_claims.claim: On the encoder task the agent with notes reached 16.1 dB versus 15.0 dB for PPO, 13.8 dB random start and 16.9 dB for calibrated-model backpropagation; Fable 5.2 beat Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.
key_claims.quote: it reached 16.1 dB, against 15.0 dB for PPO and 13.8 dB for the random start (Fig. 3c,d). The best result obtained on this experiment, 16.9 dB, came from backpropagation through a calibrated model

key_claims.claim: The agent reparametrizes the masks with a few interpretable optical parameters (lenses, prisms, aberrations) instead of pixel updates.
key_claims.quote: In both routes, a small number of interpretable parameters replace several hundred thousand pixel updates

key_claims.claim: Harness ablations on the calibrated model show more information (camera images, probes, hypotheses, notes) helps, and even with scalar reward only the agent beat PPO (71.3% vs 58.7%).
key_claims.quote: Even with the single scalar reward per candidate that the gradient-free methods receive, the agent clearly outperformed PPO.

limitations_stated.text: Each test accuracy carries finite-test-set uncertainty; run-to-run spread for runs with notes was 3.9 points.
limitations_stated.quote: The three classifier runs that received notes or general lessons from earlier sessions reached 89.2%, 91.3% and 96.8% on the test digits (mean 92.4%, standard deviation 3.9 percentage points).

notes_for_review: Applies the WSP idea to physical optical networks: a coding agent with probes, camera images and a notes file trains phase masks in situ, and the comparison includes tuned PPO/policy-gradient baselines and backpropagation through a calibrated digital twin. The headline 96.8% is the best of three runs and relies on notes from a previous session; the agent without notes reached 91.1%. Harness ablations were run on the calibrated simulator, not the hardware. The parameters edited are optical phase masks expressed as code (lenses, prisms), so this is weight programming only in a broad sense.
